thread:
Ava: Heads-up — Sales pushed a retro promotional usage credit for a set of Q2 customers. It hits Zuora as credit memos today. Quick question for month-end: do we accrue/deferral this or treat as a current period adjustment? Need recommendation for close checklist.

Maya: Need a bit more color — is this credit for past usage (billing correction) or a promo that covers future usage?

Ava: It's tagged 'promo-retro-Q2' in the billing notes. Sales says they ran a pricing experiment and decided to credit customers for usage from Apr–May (already invoiced). Total pool ~ $145k across ~30 accounts.

Luca: If it's a true billing correction (reduces previously recognized revenue) then GAAP says adjust prior period if material. Otherwise we book a catch-up in current period per our immaterial correction policy.

Jon: How does Zuora/NetSuite flow work for this? Will the credit memos auto-create reversal schedules?

BillingBot: Billing batch 2026-06-14 created credit memos: invoice_ids=[54821,54822,54903,...], total_credit=145000.00, reason="promo-retro-Q2"

Maya: Practically: 1) For each credit memo, create a negative revenue schedule entry in RCS tied to the original revenue schedule id; 2) If we decide to adjust prior period (material), file a prior-period adjustment and restate; 3) If immaterial, we book an expense or contra-revenue in June and adjust current revenue schedules.

Ava: We need a rule-of-thumb for materiality here so close team can proceed. Finance policy?

Luca: Our threshold is 5% of period revenue or $250k absolute for restatement. This $145k is below absolute but check % of Q2 recognized revenue for the affected product (could be >5%).

Jon: I'll pull product-level Q2 revenue numbers — give me 30 mins. If >5% we restate, otherwise do current-period catch-up.

Maya: If we do catch-up, recommended journal (example per credit memo):

```
# credit memo applied to customer invoice
DR Sales Returns & Allowances  12,345.67
  CR Accounts Receivable          12,345.67
# to record accounting impact (catch-up in June)
DR Revenue Adjustment (contra) 12,345.67
  CR Revenue                   12,345.67
```

Maya: If we defer (promo intended to cover future service) then instead of immediate revenue adjustment we would: create a deferred liability and amortize over remaining term. Journal example: 

```
DR Sales Returns & Allowances 12,345.67
  CR Accounts Receivable        12,345.67
DR Deferred Revenue            12,345.67
  CR Revenue                   12,345.67  # to move to deferred and amortize subsequently
```

Ava: For the affected accounts, contracts are annual and started Jan — promo covers usage already consumed (Apr–May), not future months. Sounds like billing correction.

Luca: Then it's a correction. Next step: quantify by product and compute percent of Q2 revenue. If <5% for each product, treat as current-period adjustment and book contra-revenue in June. If >=5% for any product, escalate for restatement review.

Jon: Pulled numbers — product A Q2 revenue = 1.8M, credits affecting A = 120k => 6.7% -> hits restatement threshold for product A.

Ava: Ugh. So we need to restate? That will affect Q2 close and disclosures. Who owns the restatement process?

Maya: Accounting ops owns the mechanics; reporting/FP&A owns disclosures. We'll need review by external auditors if we restate. Practical immediate action: tag all credit memos affecting product A and halt auto-posting in NetSuite revenue scheduler until we confirm.

BillingBot: Credit memos for product A: invoice_ids=[54821,54903,55010], total=120000. Posted flag=false (manual hold requested).

Ava: OK I'm putting a hold on posting and routing to Maya for calculation pack. @Maya can you assemble the schedule adjustments and proposed restatement entries? We need a sign-off matrix for audit.

Maya: On it. I'll prepare a per-account mapping, revenue schedule diffs, and GL impact table. ETA EOD. Also will note required disclosures and coordinate with FP&A.

Jon: I'll draft the disclosure language and assemble the footnote numbers after Maya's pack.

Luca: Sales ops — FYI: don't push similar promo credits without finance pre-approval. We need a standard approval flow for promo experiments that might affect revenue recognition.

Ava: Agreed. For close checklist: 1) Identify promo credit memos 2) Calculate product-level impact 3) Decide restate vs current catch-up 4) If restate -> prepare restatement worksheet + auditor notif 5) Post GL + RCS adjustments once approved

Maya: I'll add that to month-end close playbook and create a short Slack form for Sales to request retro promos going forward.

Ava: Thanks all. I'll update the close channel and flag the credit memos on the billing side. :thumbsup:

Luca: Thanks — tag me once Maya has the pack, I'll coordinate with legal/audit if needed. :ok_hand:

BillingBot: Action log: hold placed on credit memos [54821,54903,55010] by Ava at 2026-06-14T15:12:34Z

Maya: Pack in progress — will upload to /finance/month-end/docs and ping here when ready.

Ava: Closing loop — appreciate the quick turnaround.
